subject: Audit rights and SOC 2 evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Dan Miller <dan.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-22T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Audit rights and SOC 2 evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form

Rishi —

Thanks for the draft order form. Legal here at Acme has a few outstanding items we need clarity on before we can move to procurement:

- SOC 2: please confirm if you can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report (or SSAE attestation) and whether you will allow an auditor to validate controls on our behalf.
- Pen test: we need either 1) a redacted final pen test report covering findings/remediation, or 2) a scoped attestation letter plus a windowed staging access to validate fixes.
- Audit rights / inspection triggers: the MSA currently allows for for-cause inspections — we need to understand what triggers you will accept (regulatory notice, suspected breach, material incident) and what cadence looks like for scheduled evidence reviews.
- Evidence retention and escrow: can you commit to keeping evidence artifacts for 36 months and provide a mechanism for secure transfer to our auditors?

Can you put together a short playbook (what evidence we will get, how often, who to contact, and timeline expectations) and highlight any redlines from your legal team? Procurement is asking for specifics so we can slot this into our onboarding calendar.

Attached: Acme_Audit_Questionnaire.xlsx (our standard list).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we are targeting final MSA/Order Form sign-off by mid-October.

Thanks,
Dan
Senior Contracts Manager
Acme Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-22T09:40:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights and SOC 2 evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form

Team — looping you in to coordinate a response and proposed redlines. Summary of asks from Acme: SOC 2 report access, pen test report or attestation + windowed staging, for-cause inspection triggers, 36-month evidence retention, and auditor transfer mechanism.

Proposed positions (high level):
- SOC 2: provide the latest Type II report and a completed control matrix. Do NOT provide raw system logs to external auditors; offer a controlled auditor review (remote) and an on-site mediated review only under a signed NDA and reasonable notice.
- Pen test: offer a redacted executive summary + attestation letter from our third-party tester. For customers requiring more, provide a timeboxed staging window (4 hours) with scoped accounts and an on-call engineer; require an active NDA and minimal prior notice (72 hours).
- Inspection triggers: accept scheduled evidence reviews quarterly and 'for-cause' only on material incidents defined as 'confirmed data exposure affecting >1000 records or regulator subpoena'. Avoid open-ended on-demand inspections.
- Evidence retention: confirm 36 months for artifact-level artifacts (SOC reports, attestations, remediation summaries). Live logs and SIEM data remain internal; provide snapshots/exports where feasible.

Next steps: Laura — can you draft firm redline language that preserves our operational constraints but gives Acme enough assurance? Ben — please prepare a one-page technical runbook that describes what we can hand off (files, artifact formats, timeboxed staging steps). Monica — CS to draft an SLA note that covers timing for evidence delivery and escalation path.

I attached a short draft with bullet redlines to speed review (rdl-msawording-draft.docx). I'll bridge a quick call with Acme if you think it's useful.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dan Miller <dan.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-22T13:05:47-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights and SOC 2 evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your proposals:

- SOC 2: Type II plus control matrix is fine. We do need confirmation that the auditor we appoint can validate control implementation (remote is OK) and that you will engage to address access questions.
- Pen test: redacted executive summary + attestation is acceptable, but we reserve the right to request a deeper review 'for cause' if a significant security incident is suspected. In those cases, we may request temporary, scoped access to systems or full reports under a mutual NDA.
- For-cause trigger: we can accept a materiality threshold, but it must include suspected breaches that involve protected health information (PHI) regardless of record count. We cannot accept thresholds that exclude PHI incidents.
- Evidence handoff: we need a secure method to receive artifacts (SFTP or signed transfer via our compliance portal) and an acknowledgement timeline (48 hours to confirm receipt of requested files).

If you can amend the redline to reflect PHI carve-in for for-cause access and a 48-hour acknowledgement timeline for artifact transfers, procurement can move forward. Also please provide a named contact for the pen test staging (ops engineer) if we need to schedule a window.

Appreciate it — Dan

Subject: Re: Audit rights and SOC 2 evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form

Dan — thanks for the clear feedback. Quick update and proposed compromise below.

1) SOC 2 / auditor validation
We will provide the current SOC 2 Type II report and control matrix. We will permit remote auditor validation of controls; on-site mediated review is available when absolutely required by regulation, subject to an NDA, reasonable notice (7 business days), and a documented scope.

2) Pen test
We will provide a redacted pen test report and a pen test attestation letter. For-cause deeper review is acceptable where the issue involves PHI or confirmed data exposure; in those cases we will provide a timeboxed staging window and a named ops engineer to support (contact: Ben Carter, ben.carter@redwood.com). Requests for full raw reports will require an executed mutual NDA and narrow scope.

3) For-cause trigger
We will accept a carve-in for PHI incidents (i.e., suspected compromise of PHI) regardless of record count. For other incidents, the materiality threshold will be 'confirmed exposure of customer data affecting >1000 unique records' or a regulator demand. This preserves our operational constraints while addressing Acme's compliance needs.

4) Evidence retention and transfer
We commit to retaining SOC2 reports, attestations, remediation summaries, and remediation timelines for 36 months. For artifact transfer, we will use a secure SFTP endpoint and will acknowledge receipt within 48 hours. Live SIEM logs are not routinely exported; we will provide snapshots where feasible.

Next steps / owners:
- Laura: will update MSA redline language to reflect the PHI carve-in and the 48-hour artifact acknowledgement.
- Ben: will prepare the pen test runbook and confirm staging process + contact details.
- Monica/CS: will draft a short onboarding note for procurement about the evidence handoff calendar and escalation ladder.

We believe this addresses Acme's concerns while keeping our controls intact. If you agree, Rishi please confirm and we will issue an updated redline by next Tuesday (2026-09-28).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
